title: Virtual Memory Multi-Transfer Fragmentation (Page Contiguity Invalidation)
damaged_code: Requesting a single large physical device write (e.g., 40MB) using multiple fragmented virtual memory page frames without memory-mapping or direct page contiguity.
pattern: Accessing raw devices sequentially using small physical page sizes mapped non-contiguously in virtual memory.
why_bad: Forces physical devices to break up single large transfers into multiple 1MB chunks, incurring multiple seek operations and missing rotation cycles.
detection: Large block I/O sequences processed via scattered, non-contiguous page allocations.
counterexample: The hardware controller automatically supports scatter-gather I/O. `Contextual`.
fix: Use memory-mapped file access (`mmap()`) or contiguous physical page frames to coalesce large file transfers.
